title: XENIA VILLAGE BOARD
full_story:
The Xenia Village Board met in regular session last night.  The meeting started with the approval and swearing in of Terri Beckmen to fill the empty seat on the board following the appointment of Galen Garrison as mayor after the abrupt resignation of Dwight Casolari in April.

In public comments Alif Sherwani returned to give the board of trustees updates on the renovation of the village gas station.  Mr. Sherwani told trustees that the electronic computer system has been upgraded.  The next steps are to upgrade the pumps, followed by the awning and signage.

Mr. Sherwani also shared details of an incident of theft which took place and now involves the Clay County Sheriff’s office and the Illinois State Lottery Investigator.  Sherwani did not share any figures regarding the amount that was stolen.  He only remarked it was a “substantial amount.”  Sherwani once again requested the village approve a liquor license for the gas station.  Trustee’s decided to table the decision pending review of ordinances detailing the scope and powers of the villages Liquor Commissioner.

Brandon Bridges with Charleston Engineering provided Trustees with a joint funding agreement in the amount of $1,075,000 for the resurfacing of roads.  This covers 80% of the cost to resurface Church and Main Street.

Trustees discussed the state of properties in the village who have failed to comply with city ordinances.  The motion was made to send out one final notice before taking legal action.

Xenia Police Chief Jerry Burkett told trustees that he had attended two days of High risk stop and de-escalation training with the Mount Vernon Police Department.  Burkett also shared he took the police cruiser to the Gateway Way Speedway in Madison.

The Xenia Village board raised $5,430 dollars during the March 30 Ice cream social event.  Trustees also approved the Raffle license for the village Mud Bugs.

Village Superintendent Travis Lewis informed trustees that renovations on the villages lift station have been completed.

Finally, trustees discussed blocking the street for the Jaxson Green Benefit set for July 11th from noon to 5 pm with an auction to be held from 5 to 6pm.

title: NUTRIENT STEWARDSHIP FIELD DAYS
full_story:
Illinois Farm Bureau’s Nutrient Stewardship Field Days will return this summer, highlighting members’ conservation efforts throughout the state.

“Field days are an important platform for elevating the voices of those implementing unique regenerative practices,” said Bena Pegg, IFB environmental program manager.  “The farmers leading these events are mentors, sharing practical, local knowledge that helps others build more resilient, productive and sustainable operations.”

Pegg told FarmWeek these events remain part of the effort to help Illinois meet its Nutrient Loss Reduction Strategy goals but have grown into much more.  The summer Nutrient Stewardship Field Days, scheduled June through September, and will cover a range of topics, including soil health, field research, livestock integration and regenerative agriculture.

In our area on July 7th, Jasper, Clark, Cumberland and Richland County Farm Bureaus will host a bus tour to Southern Illinois University and Southern FS to learn firsthand from researchers and agronomists.  The program is an all-day event and will include breakfast, lunch and dinner.

And on August 20th, from 6 to 8 pm, the Wayne County Farm Bureau will view the Research trials at the Nutrient Loss Inhibitor Demonstration Plot.  This year’s trials focus on the effects of nitrogen stabilizers, micronutrients, humic acid and application timing.

IFB’s Nutrient Stewardship Grant Program funds the 2026 Nutrient Stewardship Field Days.  Since 2015, IFB has awarded $1.75 million to support 192 county-led nutrient stewardship projects.

Visit bit.ly/IFBFieldDays for event updates, more information about field day locations and RSVP info.

title: PLUMMER ON BUDGET
full_story:
State Senator Jason Plummer issued the following statement after Governor JB Pritzker signed the Fiscal Year 2027 state budget into law on Tuesday.

“Today, Governor Pritzker continued his eight-year pattern of taking more from taxpayers to fund a bloated, out-of-control budget that ignores the affordability crisis hitting hardworking families across Illinois.

“Since taking office, Governor Pritzker has helped balloon state spending to nearly $56 billion, a roughly 40 percent increase since 2019.  That is not leadership.  That is a complete failure to respect the people who pay the bills.

“Right now, Illinois leads the Midwest in unemployment and outmigration, and under this sort of leadership, these results will only continue: fewer opportunities, fewer employers, fewer good-paying jobs, and fewer reasons for families and young people to build their futures here.

“Illinois has tremendous resources, incredible communities, and some of the hardest-working people in the country.  But time and again, those strengths are overshadowed by Governor Pritzker’s addiction to higher spending, higher taxes, and bigger government.

“Instead of making Illinois more affordable and more competitive, this budget doubles down on the same failed policies that have driven people, jobs, and investment out of our state.”

title: CROP PROGRESS AND CONDITION
full_story:
Illinois crop growth accelerated last week following multiple storms and rounds of rainfall.

USDA estimated the portion of crops rated good to excellent statewide totaled 66% for corn and 61% for soybeans as of June 14th in its latest crop progress and condition report released Monday.  The Illinois winter wheat crop is rated 75% in good to excellent condition with 20% harvested.

There were 3.2 days suitable for fieldwork in the week ending June 14th.  Statewide, the average temperature was 76.2 degrees, 4.9 degrees above normal.  Precipitation averaged 3.3 inches, 2.18 inches above normal.  Topsoil moisture supply was rated at 4% very short, 11% short, 57% adequate, and 28% surplus.  Subsoil moisture supply was rated 4% very short, 13% short, 63% adequate, and 20% surplus.

Corn emerged reached 94%, compared to the 5-year average of 95%.  Corn condition was rated 1% very poor, 5% poor, 28% fair, 54% good, 12% excellent.

Soybeans planted reached 95%, compared to the 5-year average of 88%.  Soybeans emerged reached 89%, compared to the 5-year average of 88%.  Soybeans condition was rated 2% very poor, 5% poor, 32% fair, 50% good, and 11% excellent.

Winter wheat harvested reached 20% compared to the 5-year average of 11%.  Winter wheat headed reached 98%, compared to the 5-year average of 99%.  Winter wheat condition was rated 2% very poor, 4% poor, 19% fair, 61% good, and 14% excellent.

title: STATE POLICE CELEBRATE YEARS
full_story:
The Illinois State Police (ISP) is celebrating its 40th anniversary of certification by the Commission on Accreditation for Law Enforcement Agencies (CALEA).  CALEA is an internationally recognized gold standard in public safety excellence.

On June 15th, of 1986, ISP became the first state police agency in the United States to achieve CALEA accreditation, highlighting ISP’s vision of being one of the nation’s premier policing agencies.

“ISP’s vision, mission, and values are the foundation of everything we do, from the way we interact with the public, pursue justice through thoughtful investigations, ensure highway safety, and work to develop our Troopers and Special agents into the best officers and community caretakers possible,” said ISP Director Brendan F. Kelly.  “Forty years is an amazing feat.  I have no doubt we will continue down this path of excellence and remain one of the premier law enforcement agencies in the country.”

To become accredited, law enforcement agencies must complete a comprehensive two to three year self-assessment, including the review and revision of polices, directives, and training standards.  Agencies must also pass a CALEA site-based compliance check and attend a review committee hearing.  Reaccreditation requires on-going quality performance reviews and maintenance of agency information and statistical data.

Transparency and accountability are two areas of focus for CALEA accreditation.  In accordance with ISP’s commitment to these values, ISP shares its departmental policies, Officer Involved Investigations Dashboard, and Expressway Shooting Dashboard, publicly on its website. ISP has also simplified its civilian complaint process, allowing citizens to report their grievances against ISP officers, as well as elected officials, through Quick Links on the ISP website.  ISP’s continued efforts in these areas not only have improved community trust and engagement but have improved the work environment for the men and women of ISP.  In excess of the CALEA requirements and long before they became a CALEA category, ISP expanded its wellness and mental health services for its employees, including a full-time Peer Support team and an Employee Assistance Program.  ISP also extended paid paternity leave for Troopers to 12 weeks.

In 2024, ISP increased its starting compensation package for new Troopers to approximately $90,000 to help ensure quality cadets.  ISP offers college credit to Academy graduates at seven Illinois universities to support continued education.  ISP has also increased recruiting efforts for prior military members looking enter policing, and current certified police officers from outside agencies seeking an opportunity to join ISP.  Qualified candidates are encouraged to visit www.IllinoisTrooper.com for more information.

title: CARLYLE LAKE FIREWORKS
full_story:
The US Army Corps of Engineers at Carlyle Lake is proud to announce the return of the Fireworks Spectacular in celebration of the 250th anniversary of our nation’s independence.  Carlyle Lake is celebrating on Saturday, June 27 at Dam West Recreation Area for a full day of live music, vendors, and an unforgettable fireworks display launching from Point One at dusk.

Presented by the Carlyle Lake Fireworks Committee and the City of Carlyle, this annual occasion is made possible through funds raised by the Carlyle Lake Haunted Trail, generous local sponsors, and donations collected during the celebration.

Top viewing locations for the fireworks include the Carlyle Lake Main Dam, Dam West Recreation Area, the Dam West and Dam East boat ramps, the Dam West and Dam East spillways, Mariner’s Village Resort, and viewing from the water.  Traffic will be managed by park rangers, local law enforcement, and volunteers, with designated parking areas available at multiple locations to help ensure smooth access for visitors.  Accessible accommodations for visitors with disabilities will be available at the Dam West Boat Ramp and Lakeview Access.

The Dam Jam at Shelter Two in Dam West Recreation Area will feature live music throughout the day from The Jumpstarts at 1 pm, One-Legged Pancakes at 2:30 pm, Taylor-Huster All Stars at 4 pm, Wicked Mojo at 6 pm, and 13 Grit at 7:30 pm.

Fireworks are shot off at Point One at dusk, usually around 9:00 pm.

In addition to the Fireworks Spectacular, campground programs will be offered Friday evening, with water safety patrols active Saturday and Sunday afternoons.

title: FEDERAL SCHOLARSHIP TAX CREDIT PROGRAM
full_story:
Governor JB Pritzker has less than seven months to decide whether Illinois families in public, private or home schools can benefit from donated education money.

By January 1st the governor must choose whether to opt Illinois into the Federal Scholarship Tax Credit program, which provides a dollar-for-dollar tax credit of up to $1,700 for donations to qualifying scholarship-granting organizations.  The money could help families with such things as finding a tutor, sending their children to a different school or getting them special lessons.

Taxpayers who donate can receive the credit no matter what Pritzker decides.  But Illinois students benefit only if he says ‘yes’ to the program.

Nearly 64% of Illinois voters in 33 jurisdictions supported opting into the program in a non-binding question on the March 17th ballot.

While some lawmakers listened to Illinois voters and introduced a bill that would opt Illinois into the program, other lawmakers influenced by the Chicago Teachers Union introduced a measure to block the state from opting in.

The most recent state test scores show just over half of students were reading at grade level in spring 2025.  Only 39% were proficient in math.

The scholarship program offers families a way to provide the academic support their children need, whether at home, at their local public school or at a private school.

Instead, the scholarships are donated by taxpayers.  The credit of up to $1,700 will matter little to a billionaire but could persuade middle-income givers.

The only cost to the federal government is minimal foregone income tax revenue.  There is no cost to states, only the benefit of more help flowing directly to students.

Democratic New York Governor Kathy Hochul recently said she intends to opt in her state, as she is “supportive of the federal tax credit scholarship and its potential to help New York students and schools.”

Colorado Governor Jared Polis, also a Democrat, calls opting in a no-brainer.  “The more Democratic governors learn about it, I fully expect that most will come around and participate,” Polis said.  “Because from our perspective, it’s free money.”

Jorge Elorza, CEO of Democrats for Education Reform, has said that “if a state does not opt in, then by default, the first $1,700 in every single federal taxpayer’s taxes is going to leave your state.”  Referring to polling, Elorza said that “opting in is not just popular, it is overwhelmingly popular.”

The money can be used for educational therapies for students with disabilities.

Most students with disabilities enroll in public schools.  In the 2024-2025 school year, nearly 375,000 Illinois students with disabilities attended public schools.
